answer: The cipher escrow holds each stake, the jade settlement releases it, and the bridge audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 19% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 169 keys therefore burns that exposure 169 times over before it earns anything, since its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
